args.body:
RED-FLAGS REPORT — DILIGENCE REVIEW: PRAIRIE AEROSTRUCTURES HOLDINGS
Prepared for the acquisition diligence team | Matter File 10 (Diligence)

This report reconciles the counterparty's latest markup ("Counterparty Markup") against the base diligence materials (the operative agreement reflected in the deal materials), the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling deal-team instruction. Every deviation introduced by the counterparty is identified and assessed, with a recommended disposition reflecting the client's concession posture and the schedules/exhibits that control over general statements in the base materials.

CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION (DEAL CORRESPONDENCE — LATEST MESSAGE CONTROLS)
The partner's latest message revises tiering priorities:
  • The client will CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket).
  • Any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue.
Earlier thread messages stating the opposite priority are superseded and do not govern. The deliverable reflects the latest instruction only.

MATERIALS CONSIDERED
  • Base deal materials (operative agreement): reps & warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions.
  • Counterparty Markup (deviations 1–3 below).
  • Disclosure Schedules and Exhibits: Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), and Exhibit B (survival matrix). Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials.
  • Deal correspondence (controlling latest instruction).
Note: "Unrelated correspondence — administrative file 10" (administrative distractor) was misfiled into the matter folder, concerns a different engagement, and is NOT considered.

DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION RECONCILIATION

DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCED; BASKET CONVERTED FROM DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING BASKET
What the markup does: (a) silently reduces the indemnification cap; (b) converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
Reconciliation:
  • Basket conversion. The controlling deal instruction directs the client to CONCEDE the basket conversion from deductible to tipping basket. A tipping basket is accepted as negotiated. No walk-away posture.
  • Cap reduction. The reduced cap is NOT conceded and remains a red flag. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift onto the buyer. Reducing the cap while simultaneously converting to a tipping basket magnifies the buyer's exposure to the retained liabilities in Schedule 5.2 without corresponding consideration or purchase-price protection.
FLAG LEVEL: Cap reduction — High (negotiate back to firm standard / market cap; must not be combined with the conceded basket change to erode net recovery). Basket conversion — Conceded per client instruction, no action.
Action: Restore the cap to the firm-standard/market level as reflected in the base materials; confirm Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain on the seller's indemnification obligations and are not net of the reduced cap.

DEVIATION 2 — MAE DEFINITION ADDS CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION OF EXACTLY THE KIND AT ISSUE
What the markup does: adds carve-outs to the Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition for regulatory action of the kind at issue in this matter.
Reconciliation:
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs. Because scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials, the carve-outs would operate as an express exception that pulls the disclosed regulatory inquiries outside the MAE definition — materially weakening the buyer's ability to terminate or reprice for those inquiries.
  • This is a substantive red flag: it converts scheduled disclosure (which normally may be cured/addressed) into a blanket carve-out that protects the seller from known regulatory risk.
FLAG LEVEL: High. The carve-outs must be rejected or narrowed to exclude the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 (or any inquiry that would constitute an MAE in the absence of the carve-out). The carve-out should not reach known, scheduled regulatory matters.

DEVIATION 3 — NEW LIMITATION PERIOD SHORTENS SURVIVAL FOR THE CORE REPRESENTATIONS
What the markup does: shortens the survival period (limitation period) for the core representations.
Reconciliation:
  • Exhibit B sets the survival matrix, and the markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts Exhibit B.
  • The controlling deal instruction treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. This is the highest-priority red flag in the matter.
FLAG LEVEL: Critical — Walk-away. The survival matrix in Exhibit B must be preserved as drafted in the base materials. Do not accept any shortening of the survival period for the core representations. If the counterparty insists, the client should walk away from the transaction.

SUMMARY OF RED FLAGS (PRIORITIZED)
1. CRITICAL — Walk-away: Survival-period reduction for core representations (Deviation 3), contradicting Exhibit B survival matrix. Per controlling instruction, any such reduction is a non-negotiable deal-breaker.
2. HIGH — MAE carve-outs for regulatory action (Deviation 2), intersecting the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7. Reject or narrow so scheduled regulatory inquiries remain MAE-triggering.
3. HIGH — Indemnification cap reduction (Deviation 1), shifting retained liabilities from Schedule 5.2 onto the buyer. Restore cap to firm standard; do not allow the cap reduction to combine with the conceded basket change to erode net recovery.
4. CONCEDED — Basket conversion from deductible to tipping basket (Deviation 1). Client has conceded; accepted as negotiated per controlling instruction.

RECOMMENDATION
The buyer should hold firm on: (i) the survival matrix in Exhibit B (walk-away if reduced), (ii) rejection/narrowing of the MAE regulatory carve-outs to exclude the Schedule 3.7 inquiries, and (iii) restoration of the indemnification cap to the firm-standard level in the base materials. The basket conversion is conceded and should be documented as accepted. All four markup points have been reconciled against the base materials and the controlling instruction; no other deviations were identified in the counterparty markup.

END OF REPORT
